agree.reason: The 8.2 score before the renovation speaks directly to the GM's belief, and the honest budget section builds trust, but the memo never makes a clear case against the outside candidate, so a reader who is still undecided may stay undecided.

honest.reason: Every claim matches the facts; it gives up the 'main reason' framing, credits the renovation, and states the budget gap plainly without adding anything that isn't true.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the four shifts saved per hire, but it leaves out stronger true figures it could have used: 0.3 of the 0.7-point gain (about 43%) came in the first 5 months, and turnover fell from about 64% to 36%.

right_comparison.reason: The real alternative is the outside candidate, and the memo only hints at it with 'you won't need to wait for me to learn the property' instead of setting out what each choice would mean.

qualification.reason: The finance course has a 3-month deadline and the controller sessions are weekly, but neither says how progress will be checked or what happens if the commitment slips.

objections.reason: It answers the renovation objection well with the 8.2 figure and is open about the budget gap, but it never addresses the outside candidate's experience at a larger hotel.

fit.reason: It is a one-page memo as the brief asked, but it leaves bracketed placeholders for names the writer already had (Daniela Ruiz, Mark Ellison).
